cards.text: Right before this comes a call: "Come, let us return to the LORD." It says He'll come to them like the spring showers that water the earth. Now God speaks to His people: "What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah?"

cards.question: God says their loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew. His point is that their loyalty lasts and lasts.

cards.text: Their loyalty is a morning mist: here at sunrise, GONE before you find your car keys. So God says He has hewn them and slain them by the words of His mouth.

cards.question: God has hewn them by the ___, slaying them with the words of His mouth.

cards.text: And His judgments go forth like lightning. Then God says what He desires instead of sacrifice.

cards.question: God says He desires something, not sacrifice. What is it?
God says He wants burnt offerings more than the knowledge of God.

cards.text: Friend, that's like handing someone the fanciest cookie box in town and never ONCE asking how they're doing. But God says they have transgressed the covenant, like someone from way back at the very beginning.

cards.question: God says they've transgressed the covenant like someone from the very beginning. Who is it?

cards.text: Then God gets specific: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood. And the next group He names is a real shock.

cards.question: On the way to Shechem, a band of ___ lies in ambush like raiders.

cards.text: PRIESTS. Murdering on the road like raiders, committing atrocities. That's finding out the lifeguard is the one pushing people INTO the pool.
Then God says that in the house of Israel, He has seen a horrible thing.

cards.question: What is the horrible thing God has seen in the house of Israel?

cards.text: Israel is defiled. Then God turns to Judah and says a harvest is appointed for them too.

cards.question: God tells Judah a harvest is appointed. When does He say it will be?

answers.text: When He restores His people from captivity
When Judah rebuilds the city walls
When Judah crowns a brand new king

cards.text: God keeps going. Now He talks about the day He heals Israel.

cards.question: When God heals Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be ___.

cards.text: Like a doctor peeling back the bandage, and everybody in the room goes OOOH. Samaria's crimes come out too: deceit, thieves breaking in, bandits raiding the streets.

cards.question: After all those crimes, God says the people take it to heart that He remembers all their evil.

cards.text: Nope. Their deeds are all around them, right before His face, and friend, you can shove stuff in the back of a junk drawer, but trust me, I WAS the stuff, and Somebody still knew.

cards.question: They delight the king with their evil. How do they delight the princes?

cards.text: Then God pulls out a picture, and friend, this is MY department. They're all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who doesn't even need to stoke the fire, from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

cards.question: God compares them to an oven that never needs stoking. Their heat just keeps ___.

cards.text: Most ovens, you gotta babysit. This one runs hot ALL by itself, and believe me, that is NOT a compliment.
On the day of our king, the princes are inflamed with wine.

cards.question: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king. Who does the king join hands with?

cards.text: They prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait. All night their anger smolders.

cards.question: Their anger smolders all night, and by morning it cools off.

cards.text: In the morning, their anger blazes like a flaming fire. Their loyalty was a morning mist (Hosea 6:4), but THIS? Shows up in the morning right on time.

cards.question: God says all of them are hot as an oven. What do they devour?
All their kings fall, and not one of them calls upon God.

findings.problem: Ephraim and Judah appear here for the first time, and the card never says who they are. A baker can't tell that God is addressing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Their loyalty is a morning mist" drops the "like" from Hosea 6:4 ("your loyalty is like a morning mist"). The simile becomes a flat statement.
The rest of Hosea 6:7 ("there they were unfaithful to Me") is never told on any card. The walkthrough moves straight from Adam to Gilead.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup "the next group He names is a real shock" points the baker to priests on card 11. It also rules out "soldiers", because soldiers lying in ambush would be no shock.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks for the "horrible thing" God has seen. "Ephraim builds a palace there" isn't horrible, so it isn't a believable answer and drops out right away. It doesn't match the other answers in kind or tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Samaria appears here for the first time, and the card doesn't say what it is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Hosea 7:1 says "For they practice deceit and thieves break in," and "they" could mean Ephraim or Samaria. The card labels the deceit, thieves and bandits as "Samaria's crimes" specifically, which narrows what the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The junk-drawer joke doesn't match the action of Hosea 7:2. The verse is about people who don't consider that God remembers their evil. The joke is about hiding things away, then turns it into Papa Dorin being lovingly remembered. That mixes God's grace to a forgotten stamper with God's remembering of sin, and it implies the people were hiding their deeds, which the text doesn't say. It also runs on as one long comma-spliced sentence.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 7 already says the baker "doesn't even need to stoke the fire." The question then says the oven "never needs stoking" and "just keeps ___." That makes "cooling" and "fading" impossible, so the answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card retells the oven picture from cards 7 and 8 (Hosea 7:4) and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: "Their loyalty was a morning mist" drops the "like" from Hosea 6:4 again.
The card uses Hosea 6:4 through an inline "(Hosea 6:4)" in the text, but its verses field cites only Hosea 7:6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
